notes: Features are the producer's aggregate (core.calc_all_features_v3 on raw z), read as stored. This experiment is the producer's event-level aggregate, a censored sample: it leaves out every event with a single hit (its spatial SDs are undefined), so its momentum bins are not balanced, the lowest bins lose the most events, and their mean response is biased high, because single-hit showers deposit the least. The hit-level file of the same run keeps them.

avg_phi is the file's arithmetic mean of the hits' azimuths, kept for parity; an azimuth wraps, so it is not a direction and is never drawn as one. Its circular mean and angular_spread_circ need Σ cos φ and Σ sin φ per event, which only the hit files carry.

Centroids are energy-weighted (core.py:491-497); std_r and the SDs inside angular_spread are sample SDs (ddof = 1); num_hits counts rows. angular_spread adds a linear SD of φ, which the ±π cut inflates; angular_spread_circ uses the circular SD √(−2 ln R̄) instead.

Depth in the absolute frame is quoted below the front face, z − 3649 mm. The volume, both densities, centroid_z and the radii use raw z, as the producer computed them, so the volume there is not a geometric volume.
core.py floors width, height, depth and depth range at 10⁻⁶ mm; a floored factor makes the volume tiny and both densities enormous.
Momentum classes are the producer's 1 GeV bins (its integer bin column).

Quartiles are np.percentile's linear interpolation, as pandas' describe(); SD is the sample SD (ddof = 1) and sd_population the ddof = 0 form, for comparison with the notebook. The mean's 95% interval is Student-t, t(0.975, N − 1) · SD/√N; the SD's is the χ² interval, which assumes Gaussian values and is too narrow for a heavy tail.

sd_se = SD/√(2(N − 1)) is the SD's own standard error under the same Gaussian assumption; c4(N) = E[s]/σ is the bias the ddof = 1 SD keeps (it still runs 11.4% low at N = 3); robust marks N ≥ 20. All three use the N each feature actually described, after non-finite and excluded values, and so does the note each cell takes from notes_by_n at its own N - N = 2 is one degree of freedom.
Azimuths get a circular summary - mean direction, mean resultant length R̄, circular SD and the Rayleigh p - and no linear mean, SD or quartile; min and max lie on (−π, π].
Below N = 20 the quartiles interpolate between individual events (1–2 GeV, 5–6 GeV, 7–8 GeV, 12–13 GeV, 15–16 GeV, 19–20 GeV).
